subject: CrystalWave — Dedicated GPU pool: orchestration & handoff
messages:
From: Aisha Verma <aisha@crystalwave.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dan Keller <dan.k@crystalwave.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry — CrystalWave

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We have internal approval to move forward with reserved dedicated capacity for inference (primary use: multi-model text-generation + embeddings for our consumer-facing features). High-level asks:

- EU residency requirement (data must stay in eu-west-1).
- Baseline throughput target: ~400 rps for short-form generation (avg 128 tokens), burst to 1,200 rps for traffic spikes during marketing campaigns.
- Models: mix of 7B and 13B open models, plus a quantized 30B variant for some heavy routes.
- Expected go-live window: end of Feb.

Please share an outline of the provisioning plan, autoscale/burst recommendations, and any network/VPC requirements. I attached our initial requirements spreadsheet.

Best,
Aisha

--
Aisha Verma
Head of ML Platforms, CrystalWave
aisha@crystalwave.ai
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Verma <aisha@crystalwave.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 13:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry — CrystalWave

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear requirements and the spreadsheet (received). Quick confirmation and next steps:

- Region: we can provision an eu-west-1 dedicated pool and lock data residency to that region.
- Initial sizing: propose a baseline pool sized for ~500 rps steady-state to give overhead for model loading, with a burst band to cover up to 1,200 rps via burst slots and autoscale.
- Autoscale approach: continuous short-window scale-up for predictable ramp + reserved burst credits for rapid spikes (we'll propose numbers below).
- Network: we need a VPC peering or private link + CIDR/IPs, and access to your KMS for key exchange if you want customer-managed keys.

Can you confirm: concurrency per request (how many tokens on average/long tail), SLO for p95 latency, and whether all model weights must be pinned to the dedicated pool or if some can be routed to a regional hosted fallback?

I added Karthik and Marissa — Karthik will propose the technical autoscale and pooling profile; Marissa will coordinate the implementation milestones and CS handoff. I attached a template SOW and activation CSV we typically use.

Thanks,
Evelyn

--
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Aisha Verma <aisha@crystalwave.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 08:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry — CrystalWave

Hi Aisha, quick technical notes after reviewing the sheet:

- Pool topology: 3-node minimum to allow rolling restarts + shard distribution (we'll provision homogeneous GPU instances tuned for quantized 30B inference).
- Baseline sizing rationale: 500 rps baseline assumes batching efficiency and prefix KV cache for repeated prompts. We'll set target token throughput per GPU and translate to instance counts in the SOW.
- Autoscale: propose a layered policy —
  * Steady autoscale (scale by observed 1-min qps with conservative headroom).
  * Fast burst lane (pre-warmed burst capacity: reserve 20% of pool as burst slots convertible to on-demand nodes for 10 min bursts).
  * Fallback routing: if quantized 30B saturates, route lower-priority traffic to hosted fallback (same region) to protect p95 for 7B/13B routes.
- Cost control: set token-rate throttles per route and preferential queuing for high-priority API keys.

Requirements from your infra team: VPC peering details, egress rules for health probes (we use specific IPs), and whether you require mutual TLS for control-plane RPCs.

I'll attach a quick sketch of the autoscale window parameters and instance recommendations.

-karthik

Thanks team — adding the implementation plan and a compact milestone timeline:

- Week 1 (Jan 22–26): Contract final, final SOW sign-off, exchange of VPC and KMS details.
- Week 2 (Jan 29–Feb 2): Pool provisioning in eu-west-1, initial image bake + model artifact staging.
- Week 3 (Feb 5–9): Integration testing, latency tuning, and pre-production soak.
- Week 4 (Feb 12–16): Canary cutover and go/no-go runbook; go-live Feb 17 target.

Action items for CrystalWave: share CIDR ranges, a test API key, and a small prompt set for quality checks. I'll be primary CS contact for onboarding; Sean will own runbook and ops liaison during cutover.

Attachments: activation-milestones.csv (milestones + owners), SOW_CrystalWave_v1.pdf (draft).

Marissa

Thanks — attaching our network diagram (network_diagram_v2.png) and an updated CIDR block list. A few clarifications:

- We require KMS control for data-at-rest encryption; we can provide a customer-managed key in eu-west-1.
- For the burst lane: we'd prefer burst to be limited to 15 minutes max per window, and to cap monthly burst spend to a contractual limit — can you include a soft throttle in the SOW?
- Can you confirm your health-check egress IPs and whether the peering supports AWS PrivateLink?

Aisha / Dan — great, thanks for the network diagram and the constraints. Quick recap and confirmed next steps before the CS handoff meeting next Tue (calendar invite just sent):

- KMS: CrystalWave will provide a customer-managed key in eu-west-1. We'll document key rotation and access in the SOW.
- Burst policy: we'll set burst slot TTL to 15 minutes and add a soft monthly spend cap. We'll include monitoring alerts for spend and an auto-throttle if thresholds approach the cap.
- Health checks & peering: we support AWS PrivateLink and will send the egress IPs and port list in a follow-up note (expected tomorrow).
- Milestones: Marissa to kick off the activation tracker on Jan 22 once SOW is signed; Karthik and Sean to run the provisioning and ops readiness steps.

Links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/DW-2028-0132) — please review and confirm SOW redlines before the DocuSign send.
